By being able to produce a signal accurate to the original using only a small portion of the total data, analysis of these samples would greatly reduce in time and cost, allowing for these reconstructions to be made more rapidly. Creating a program to investigate the random sensing matrix and determine which of the values in the original x vector will be used to create the measurement vector could prove incredibly useful by making this short analysis time possible and applicable. Knowing which few random samples to analyze and being able to input only those values so the algorithm could calculate the recreated signal would be further steps into making this full process successful. This project has shown that one dimensional data collected from emission collectors is sparse in the time domain, making compressed sensing not only possible, but successful in being able to make a faithful reconstruction of the original signal by using only 20% of the total measurement amount, proving our hypothesis. Application of this research can lead to reduced analysis costs of future collected air tubes, reducing analytical cost for Savannah River National Laboratory without sacrificing valuable data. V.
